answer: A registry can price entry as a climb where each new key from one funding root pays more than the last: the k-th identity posts k squared times 100 POA bond in escrow for 8 epochs, so twenty clones must lock 400 times one honest deposit. Provenance is read from history, never declared: canary audit tasks test each key, and peers whose accuracy correlates above 0.7 are folded into one cluster and billed on the same ladder. An ocean of keys under one root still drains one velvet purse, and one exposed plume burns the whole escrow.
